stories.headline: Franco-Ukrainian AI air-defense startup Alta Ares raises €50M Series A to scale drone interceptors

key_facts.fact: Alta Ares raised a €50M Series A led by Air Street Capital, with Cherry Ventures, OTB Ventures and Harpoon Ventures participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Alta Ares, the French startup building AI-powered air defence systems, has raised a €50m Series A to ramp up the production of its technology. The round was led by European solo GP fund Air Street Capital, and included London-based investor Cherry Ventures, Polish VC OTB Ventures and US firm Harpoon Ventures.

key_facts.fact: The startup, founded in 2024, builds AI-powered systems to detect, identify and intercept enemy drones and missiles, and says its products are already deployed in active conflict zones in Europe and the Middle East.
key_facts.excerpt: Alta Ares, which launched at the start of 2024, is building systems that can detect, identify and intercept enemy aircraft, as well as the AI software suite to power those systems. Alta Ares says it differentiates itself from competitors because its products are currently deployed in active conflict zones, including in Europe and the Middle East.

key_facts.fact: Co-founder and CEO Hadrien Canter says three teams are working with militaries in three conflict zones where Alta Ares systems are currently intercepting targets.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We're operationally deployed right now, which is not the case of every hot player in the game,' says Hadrien Canter, cofounder and CEO of Alta Ares. 'We have three teams working with the military in three conflict zones, where our systems are currently intercepting.'

key_facts.fact: Alta Ares operates two interceptor classes: a short-range system aimed at Iranian Shahed-style drones and a medium-range interceptor for cruise missiles and glide bombs.
key_facts.excerpt: Alta Ares develops one system designed for a short-range radius and specialising in intercepting threats like Iranian Shahed drones, and another medium-range interceptor designed for cruise missiles and glide bombs.

key_facts.fact: The €50M will be used mainly to scale production, plus hiring and international expansion across France and Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Les 50 millions d'euros levés par Alta Ares financeront des recrutements, le développement international de la société et le renforcement de ses capacités industrielles en France et en Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: Alta Ares' product stack includes Pixel Lock for embedded detection and tracking, Gamma for autonomous interceptor guidance, X-Lock for short-range drone interception and Black Bird for faster aerial threats; in early 2026 it tested Black Bird at -25°C in Estonia, reaching 450 km/h.
key_facts.excerpt: Its stack includes Pixel Lock for embedded detection, tracking, and terminal guidance; Gamma for autonomous interceptor guidance; X-Lock for short-range drone interception; and Black Bird for faster aerial threats. … The company reported three consecutive flights, ground temperatures of -17 degrees Celsius and -25 degrees Celsius at altitude, and a top recorded speed of 450 km/h.

stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview turns disclosed vulnerabilities into working exploits in hours, not weeks

key_facts.fact: Anthropic researchers ran Claude Mythos Preview against 18 Firefox security patches and got 8 working code-execution exploits, with the first exploit produced in under an hour of Mozilla releasing the patch.
key_facts.excerpt: Across 18 recent Firefox security patches, Claude Mythos Preview, our most capable model, built 8 working code-execution exploits autonomously... Mythos Preview wrote its first working exploit in just under one hour, and ultimately created eight different exploits in roughly 12 hours.

key_facts.fact: On 21 Windows kernel patches with no source code available, Mythos Preview produced 18 proof-of-concept crashes (first in 31 minutes, all within six hours) and 8 full exploit chains escalating a low-privilege user to SYSTEM level.
key_facts.excerpt: In testing against 21 Windows kernel vulnerabilities, Mythos Preview developed proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits for 18 vulnerabilities... The model later generated eight exploit chains that elevated a low-privileged user to SYSTEM-level access. It produced its first proof-of-concept in 31 minutes and generated all 18 within six hours.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic estimates the Windows kernel privilege-escalation chains cost roughly $1,700-$2,200 in API credits, averaging about $2,000 per exploit.
key_facts.excerpt: exploits, at a cost of $1,700 in API credits—an average of about $2,000 per privilege escalation. The binding constraint to N-days is now just a few thousand dollars and API access

key_facts.fact: Anthropic concludes that publicly available models with safeguards disabled can also build exploits, though fewer than Mythos Preview, and argues that 'N-day has become dangerously misleading. N-hour is closer to the reality we now operate in.'
key_facts.excerpt: The researchers argued that exploit-development timelines have shortened to the point where the term 'N-day' may no longer accurately reflect the threat. 'N-day has become dangerously misleading. N-hour is closer to the reality we now operate in,' the researchers concluded.

key_facts.fact: For Firefox, the patched stable release was still 18 days away when Mythos Preview produced its first working exploit from the patch diff.
key_facts.excerpt: Mythos Preview had its first exploit within an hour of Mozilla issuing the patch for it—while it would've been 18 days before the patched Firefox 148 was even released.

stories.headline: Apple unveils AFM Cloud Pro running on Nvidia Blackwell B200 GPUs inside Google Cloud at WWDC

key_facts.fact: Apple revealed at WWDC that its most powerful new model, Apple Foundation Model Cloud Pro, will run in the cloud on Nvidia GPUs inside Google Cloud, extending Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple AI executive Amar Subramanya said that AFM Cloud Pro is comparable to Google's Gemini frontier models. It will run in the cloud on Nvidia GPUs, which are part of Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure, Apple officials said.

key_facts.fact: The cloud tier uses Nvidia Blackwell B200 GPUs and turns on Nvidia's confidential computing feature, which encrypts data while it is being processed on the chip.
key_facts.excerpt: The rebuilt Siri runs on a custom 1.2-trillion-parameter model built on Google's Gemini technology, hosted on Google Cloud servers powered by Nvidia Blackwell B200 GPUs. … Nvidia's confidential computing feature encrypts data while it is being processed on the Blackwell GPUs, adding a hardware-level safeguard on top of the contractual one.

key_facts.fact: AFM Cloud Pro is the only one of Apple's five new foundation models optimized for Nvidia GPUs instead of Apple Silicon, and adds roughly 10% in text response quality, 14% in image understanding and 14% on math tasks over AFM Cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: AFM 3 Cloud Pro is the most powerful server model for the most demanding use cases: agentic tool use and complex reasoning. Compared with AFM 3 Cloud, it adds another roughly 10 percent in response quality for text and 14 percent in image understanding; on math tasks it gains 14 percent. Notably, as the only one of the five models, AFM 3 Cloud Pro was optimized not for Apple Silicon but for NVIDIA GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Apple says it routes Siri queries through three tiers: simple tasks on-device, moderate ones to Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers, and the heaviest to Nvidia GPUs in Google Cloud, with requests "never stored" and inaccessible to anyone.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple now routes Siri queries through three layers. Simple tasks stay on-device using Apple's own models. Moderately complex requests go to Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers. … 'We use none of the models that Google deploys to its customers,' software chief Craig Federighi said at a WWDC media event. 'Your requests are completely private to you. They're never stored. They're never accessible to anyone.'

key_facts.fact: This marks Apple's first use of Nvidia chips in roughly a decade, with training done on Google's cloud TPUs while serving runs on Nvidia GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: While Apple and Nvidia have a history… it is the first time that the company has [used Nvidia chips in years].

key_facts.fact: Apple's contract reportedly bars Google from training future models on Apple user data, and Apple says Google receives no Apple user data through the arrangement.
key_facts.excerpt: Crucial to the privacy story Apple is determined to keep: user data would 'never be stored or shared — not even with Apple,' and Google confirmed that it receives no Apple user data.

stories.headline: Federal judge in Boston strikes down Trump's $100K H-1B visa fee as an unlawful tax

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Leo Sorokin in Boston vacated Trump's $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa applications, ruling that the policy violated the federal Administrative Procedure Act and the Constitution
key_facts.excerpt: A federal judge on Monday vacated President Donald Trump's $100,000 fee for employers' H-1B visa applications for highly-skilled foreign workers. The policy implementing the high fee on the visas for workers in a specialty occupation violated the federal Administrative Procedure Act and the Constitution, Judge Leo Sorokin declared in the ruling in U.S. District Court in Boston.

key_facts.fact: Sorokin concluded the payment is functionally a tax that Congress had not delegated to the executive branch, writing 'the substance and application of the $100,000 payment reveal that it is a tax, regardless of what the payment is called'
key_facts.excerpt: The Boston-based judge wrote 'the substance and application of the $100,000 payment reveal that it is a tax, regardless of what the payment is called.'

key_facts.fact: The ruling came in a lawsuit filed by 20 Democratic state attorneys general; Trump implemented the fee via a presidential proclamation in September, arguing the H-1B program was being misused through 'large-scale replacement of American workers'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump implemented the $100,000 fee in a presidential proclamation last September. He argued that the H-1B visa program was being misused and undermining U.S. economic and national security through the 'large-scale replacement of American workers.'

key_facts.fact: The judge cited the Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling striking down Trump's emergency-law tariffs, applying the same logic that the president lacks authority to levy a tax under immigration law
key_facts.excerpt: The judge cited the US Supreme Court's February ruling striking down Trump's sweeping tariffs he pursued under a law meant for use in national emergencies. Under the logic of the justices' decision in that case, Trump similarly had no authority under immigration law to levy a tax, Sorokin said.

key_facts.fact: The fee dramatically suppressed demand: as of February 15, US Citizenship and Immigration Services had received just 85 payments of the $100,000 fee, the administration disclosed in March filings
key_facts.excerpt: The increase in fees has discouraged H-1B visa requests, according to court filings. As of February 15, US Citizenship and Immigration Services had received just 85 payments of the $100,000 fee, the administration said in a March filing.

key_facts.fact: White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers said the administration would appeal, noting that a federal judge in Washington DC had upheld a similar order in December
key_facts.excerpt: 'The H-1B program has been abused for decades, and President Trump finally took action to fix it. A federal judge in Washington already upheld a nearly identical order, and the Administration is confident this order will be reversed on appeal,' Rogers said.

stories.headline: Iran and Israel halt strikes at Trump's request after first fire exchange since April truce

key_facts.fact: Iran fired nearly 30 missiles at Israel; Israel struck military sites in Iran, marking the first exchanged strikes since a ceasefire began in early April
key_facts.excerpt: Iran fired nearly 30 missiles at Israel, according to the Israeli military, while Israel struck military sites in the Islamic republic.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Khatam Al-Anbiya Central Headquarters announced a halt to strikes, framing it as a 'completed operation' delivering a 'painful response' over Israeli strikes on Beirut's Dahiyeh district, while warning of 'far more intense and crushing' retaliation if Israel attacks again
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's military central command has announced a halt to its strikes against Israel, declaring it had delivered a 'painful response' to Israel over strikes on Beirut's Dahiyeh district -- but warned that any continuation of Israeli aggression would bring 'far more intense and crushing' retaliation.

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on Truth Social that both sides were seeking an immediate ceasefire and said negotiators were in the 'final throes' of a Middle East peace deal; an Israeli official said Israel halted strikes on Iran at Trump's request
key_facts.excerpt: The White House confirmed that Trump had called Netanyahu to discuss the crisis. An Israeli official said Israel had halted its strikes at his request.

key_facts.fact: Netanyahu said 'fire is on hold' against Iran but warned that if Tehran 'make the mistake of resuming attacks against us, we will respond with full force'
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a short video released by his office on June 8 that 'fire is on hold' against Iran, after Tehran ended its attacks on Israel. But speaking for the first time after Iran launched missiles at Israel, he warned that should Tehran 'make the mistake of resuming attacks against us, we will respond with full force.'

key_facts.fact: Iran's initial attack on Sunday evening was retaliation for Israeli strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, which Tehran views as a violation of the US-Iran ceasefire that requires halting hostilities in Lebanon
key_facts.excerpt: Iran launched its first attack on Israel in several weeks on Sunday evening in retaliation for Israeli strikes on the southern suburbs of Lebanon's capital Beirut.

key_facts.fact: Despite the pause between Iran and Israel, Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 14 people on Monday, according to the Lebanese health ministry; Israel said offensive operations against Hezbollah would continue 'at full force'
key_facts.excerpt: But violence continued in southern Lebanon, where Israeli strikes killed at least 14 people on Monday, according to the Lebanese health ministry.

stories.headline: Meta launches $115M America's Workforce Academy with job guarantees to staff AI data center buildout

key_facts.fact: Meta is committing $115 million in the first year to America's Workforce Academy, a free skilled-trades training program with a guaranteed job for every graduate.
key_facts.excerpt: The parent company of Facebook and Instagram is creating the America's Workforce Academy (AWA) with an initial investment of $115 million in the program's first year. It will start with pilot locations in Louisiana, Ohio, Indiana and Texas this year.

key_facts.fact: Meta calls it the largest private-sector commitment to skilled trades training with a job guarantee in US history.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta said in its announcement that this initiative is the largest private-sector commitment to the skilled trades with a job guarantee in U.S. history.

key_facts.fact: The four- to five-week bootcamp covers power generation, grid modernization and data center construction; pilots launch in Indianapolis, Baton Rouge, Houston and Columbus, with the first cohort in Baton Rouge.
key_facts.excerpt: America's Workforce Academy will teach workers about 'power generation, grid modernization and data center construction.' … The academy will be operated in four U.S. cities — Indianapolis, Indiana; Baton Rouge, Louisiana; Houston, Texas; and Columbus, Ohio. The academy's first cohort will be trained in Baton Rouge.

key_facts.fact: Meta covers tuition, airfare, lodging and pays a daily stipend; graduates earn an NCCER credential plus an America's Workforce Certificate, both portable across employers.
key_facts.excerpt: Graduates will receive two credentials after training with the academy, with one from the National Center for Construction Education and Research (NCCER) and an America's Workforce Certificate, all without paying a single dollar.

key_facts.fact: Meta says it expects to extend roughly 3,300 job offers to graduates in the program's first year; partners include Associated Builders and Contractors and CBRE.
key_facts.excerpt: We're launching in Louisiana, Ohio, Indiana, and Texas in 2026, partnering with Associated Builders and Contractors and CBRE to deliver this at scale. In our first year, we expect to extend approximately 3,300 job offers to graduates.

key_facts.fact: The program lands amid a US construction shortage of roughly 349,000 workers this year and follows Meta's recent layoff of 8,000 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: By one estimate, the construction industry is short 349,000 new workers this year amid surging investment in AI infrastructure, and data center projects tend to create more temporary than permanent positions. Last month, Meta laid off 8,000 workers amid heavy spending on artificial intelligence.

stories.headline: OpenAI confidentially files S-1 with SEC, joining Anthropic and SpaceX in IPO queue

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on June 8 that it had recently submitted a confidential S-1 to the SEC and was disclosing the filing because it expected the news to leak.
key_facts.excerpt: We recently submitted a confidential S-1. We expect it to leak so we're just announcing it. We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI was last valued at more than $850 billion after a $122 billion funding round in March 2026 and had been targeting a potential public debut as soon as Q4 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The artificial intelligence company, which is valued at more than $850 billion, has been gearing up to go public as soon as the fourth quarter of this year.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the filing process for OpenAI's potential listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the filing process ahead of a potential fall listing, according to The Wall Street Journal.

key_facts.fact: The filing comes a week after Anthropic submitted its own confidential S-1 on June 1, having closed a $65 billion round at a $965 billion valuation, and days before SpaceX is set to start trading.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic filed its own confidential S-1, roughly a week earlier. Anthropic recently closed a $65 billion round at a valuation of $965 billion. That figure pushed it past OpenAI. SpaceX leads the group. It is targeting a June 12 Nasdaq debut.

stories.headline: Pentagon adds Alibaba, Baidu, BYD, Nio and dozens more to Chinese military companies list

key_facts.fact: On June 8 the US Department of Defense published an updated Section 1260H list designating Alibaba, Baidu, BYD, Nio, WuXi AppTec, Unitree, TP-Link, JA Solar, Trina Solar, CALB, EVE Energy, Hesai, RoboSense, BOE and CATL among more than 60 additions as 'Chinese military companies'
key_facts.excerpt: Among the most prominent additions were e-commerce giant Alibaba, search and AI company Baidu, electric vehicle manufacturers BYD and Nio, pharmaceutical research and manufacturing company WuXi AppTec, robot maker Unitree, networking equipment maker TP-Link and solar companies JA Solar and Trina Solar. The list also included battery makers CALB and EVE Energy, lidar firms Hesai and RoboSense, and display-panel manufacturer BOE Technology Group.

key_facts.fact: With these additions, the Pentagon has now declared all three of China's top AI champions (Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent) as supporting the People's Liberation Army; Tencent was added in 2025 and has been seeking removal
key_facts.excerpt: With the move, the US has now declared that three of China's artificial intelligence champions – Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent Holdings – aid the Asian country's armed forces. Tencent was added to the list in 2025 and has been seeking its removal.

key_facts.fact: Starting June 30, 2026, the FY 2024 National Defense Authorization Act will prohibit DoD from entering into or renewing direct contracts with listed entities; indirect-procurement restrictions take effect in 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Starting June 30, the FY 2024 National Defense Authorization Act will prohibit DOD from entering into or renewing contracts for goods or services directly with listed entities. The same restrictions will apply to indirect goods or services starting a year from now.

key_facts.fact: The designation does not impose sanctions or block US trading but creates reputational and supply-chain risk; the list now includes more than 100 businesses, and an earlier version published briefly in February was withdrawn before being formally reissued
key_facts.excerpt: Those companies were on a previous update of the list that was posted briefly in February before being withdrawn minutes later. [...] First published in 2021, the 1260H list now includes more than 100 businesses accused of working with the Chinese military.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba called the designation baseless and said it would 'take all available legal action'; Baidu 'categorically' rejected the designation and WuXi AppTec called its listing 'incorrect'
key_facts.excerpt: Several other companies added to the list offerable similar pushback. Alibaba said there was 'no basis' for its inclusion; Baidu 'categorically' rejected the designation; WuXi AppTec called its listing 'incorrect'. Others, including BYD and battery makers CATL and Eve Energy, have yet to issue responses.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon's basis for Nio's designation cited direct and indirect SASAC affiliation and classification as a military-civil fusion contributor; for BYD, the basis was that the company operates within a military-civil fusion enterprise zone, without evidence of direct PLA contracting or technology transfer
key_facts.excerpt: For Nio, the filing cites direct and indirect affiliation with SASAC—China's state assets regulator—and classification as a military-civil fusion contributor linked to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. For BYD, the basis is that it operates within a military-civil fusion enterprise zone. Neither designation involves evidence of active military contracting, direct weapons supply or documented technology transfer to the People's Liberation Army.
